"# Extension / runtime protocol v1

Owner .1.5; design contract, not running service or production security acceptance.

## Two independent routes

Model MVP: webview -> host IPC -> TypeScript model/control-plane adapters -> Scaleway.
No Python install/startup required. Exports use external credential references and
remain runnable outside extension. Advanced agents: host -> local authenticated
HTTP runtime -> explicitly configured Strands -> approved inference/tools. Model
deployment uses control plane, not Strands. Hosted agent = our application, not a
presumed native Scaleway CreateAgent service.

## Local launch, credential resolution and authentication

Host resolves reviewed executable, Python environment and package-lock identity.
Launch only trusted pinned runtime entry point with no workspace-selected argv/cwd
or inherited secret/proxy/provider environment. Runtime listens on exactly 127.0.0.1
(random OS-assigned port); ::1 alternative requires explicitly negotiated address.
Host generates at least 256-bit random per-instance capability and bootstrap nonce.
Pass them through dedicated inherited anonymous pipe, never argv/env/workspace/logs.
Runtime replies on bootstrap pipe with nonce, instance ID, address/port and supported
versions; host validates address and launched process identity. Bootstrap pipe closes
after bounded setup. Logs/stderr are separate sanitized streams, never protocol.

Every route, including health/status/events, requires Authorization: Bearer runtime
capability and exact expected Host (IP:port). No browser Origin accepted on local
host-to-host API; CORS off; no query token, redirects or unauthenticated probes.
Runtime capability is not Scaleway credential or effect authority. Reject remote
peers, userinfo/fragment destinations, wildcard binds and uncontrolled proxies.
Same-user/host compromise remains a residual risk; module boundary is not isolation.

Provider credentials resolve via host/runtime owned external broker using purpose-
scoped opaque references. For local runtime, credential provisioning uses a reviewed
private IPC secret broker, not run/spec/event/HTTP JSON bodies; authenticate child
identity and bind secret to allowed canonical provider origin/path/scope/generation.
No provider credential in webview, exports, evidence or telemetry. No generic remote
secret-fetch endpoint. Broker implementation is .4.2; until verified, live execution
disabled. Hosted deployment needs separate workload/tenant credential/auth decisions
under .1.6/.5.3, never reuse local bearer as public authentication.

## HTTP route table (all prefixed /v1)

| Method / path | Body or query | Result |
|---|---|---|
| POST /runs | launch body, Idempotency-Key header matching body | 202 accepted, binding and sequence |
| GET /runs/{run_id} | binding verified from server context; version header | 200 status |
| POST /runs/{run_id}/cancel | cancel body with full binding | 202 cancel_ack; no rollback claim |
| GET /runs/{run_id}/events | after_sequence plus version header | authenticated SSE |

get_run/events schema objects describe client internal command before route encoding;
GET has no JSON body. request_id uses X-Request-Id and contract version
X-Contract-Version: 1.0.0. Only run ID and after_sequence may be query/path data;
mandate/credentials never URLs. Last-Event-ID if sent must equal after_sequence;
conflict is 400. Status/event reads require authorization to that run/binding, not
only knowledge of run ID. No new run created by read/reconnect.

Error envelope: 400 invalid_request, 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden, 409 scope/
stale/idempotency conflict, 410 replay_unavailable, 413 payload limit, 422 unsupported
version/feature, 429 bounded queue limit, 503 ledger/service unavailable. Safe error
code/message/retry disposition only; no provider bodies, secrets or stack traces.
401/403/409/unknown outcome never trigger inference fallback/retry.

## Launch and idempotency

1. Host validates spec/current capabilities and reviews data/effects/budget.
2. Host authority registry issues immutable expiring mandate bound to full scope,
   revisions and tool set. request body contains only opaque mandate ref and binding
   claims; runtime verifies exact equality to trusted registry, not approved=true.
   Same-user client with runtime token cannot mint mandates. Runtime instance auth
   and grant lookup are separate controls. Missing ledger/registry fails closed.
3. Atomically reserve run under (issuer, scope revision, idempotency key), binding
   canonical launch digest. Identical duplicate returns original run; different
   digest returns 409. Persist before acknowledgment. Keys retained for run lifetime
   and unresolved effects; no eviction that permits replay after crash.
4. No paid send before durable budget reservation/current epoch dispatch barrier.
   Grant ceilings intersect requested limits; expired/refunded-unknown is deny.
5. Execute Strands once, normalize events, then finalize outcome.

Ordinary file/spec/run state cannot supply grants. Bootstrap authorization provisioning
requires authenticated host-controlled IPC registry, not arbitrary runtime /mandates
POST. Hosted trusted issuer design remains a hosting prerequisite.

## Events and reconstruction

SSE event: runtime-event; id: monotonic per-run sequence; data: one JSON schema event.
Event ID is opaque stable unique identity, SSE ID equals numeric sequence. Heartbeats
are SSE comments, no run authority. Authenticated stream is read-only. Explicit
bounded replay window; clients may reconnect to existing run with cursor, never resend
launch. Gap/evicted cursor returns replay_unavailable and requires status consultation.

One run.started first, consecutive sequence; binding immutable for all events.
Terminal exactly once, last in the run stream. Event duplicate accepted only as an
identical replay; differing payload under same sequence/ID is integrity failure.
Unknown event/version is rejected, not ignored as success. Resume validators seed
prior binding/sequence/terminal from trusted status/history; fixture validator tests
full streams only. Live metadata timestamps are informational, not ordering authority.

model.attempt precedes related text/tool/usage events. attempt IDs unique; corrections
share budget and physical counter, do not restart agent. Each tool call has proposal,
policy decision, approved dispatch and result with stable call ID; event proposal alone
is not dispatch. This schema intentionally omits raw args/results and internal grants.
Tool result unknown freezes related effects; no automatic replay. Count each physical
send atomically; event presence alone does not prove a send did/did not occur.

usage.updated contains latest full attempt total, never cumulative snapshots summed.
Settle attempt exactly once by durable attempt ID; reconcile additional newer usage
without double charging/refunds. Enforce total=input+output, monotonic verified counts,
known price/currency and upward rounded integer microunits. Unknown/malformed/regressing
usage retains reservation and freezes further affected effects. terminal succeeded
requires complete output, completed remote result and known settled usage; failed or
cancelled may be partial and independently remote_outcome=unknown. JSON validated
means schema-valid, not business truth. No native structured output baseline.

## Cancellation, stale results and restart

Cancel revokes run epoch via shared dispatcher barrier, prohibits new effects and
requests local Strands/process stop. cancel_ack means request accepted, not remote
abort; terminal reports partial output/unknown billing honestly. Revocation on
trust/key/scope/spec changes uses same barrier. Never refund an ambiguous send.
Late provider results may update separate reconciliation records but never reactivate
terminal run authority or mutate active UI from another binding.

Restart rotates capability/instance ID; no old-run resume under old token. Persist
intents/outstanding reservations and reconcile before fresh reviewed execution.
No durable ledger => not eligible for production paid/tool execution. Session data
stores no active mandates/secrets and cannot authorize resume. External stores need
separate scope/encryption/retention approval. No default telemetry.

## Scope of executable checks

Shared schema/sequence fixtures validate structure, basic full-stream ordering,
terminal/unknown consistency in Python and TypeScript, not actual HTTP server,
secret broker, ledger, idempotency/revoke races, replay retention, isolation or
production adapter behavior. Those remain .3.2/.3.6/.4.2/.4.3/.5.x implementation
gates. No claim of complete Agent Builder IPC, schema migration or digest codegen.

"### NATS trigger

A NATS trigger is a mechanism that connects a container to a [NATS](/nats/concepts/#nats-messaging-system) subject and invokes the container automatically whenever a message is published to the subject.

For each message that is sent to a NATS subject, the NATS trigger reads the message and invokes the associated container with the message as the input parameter.

## Protocol

Serverless Containers supports **http1** (default) and **http2** (`h2c`). Use HTTP/2 if your container application is configured to listen for HTTP/2 requests, such as a **gRPC** service or a web server that uses HTTP/2 features like multiplexing, otherwise, HTTP/1 is recommended.

gRPC is supported on Serverless Containers, as long as you have enabled http2 (`h2c`) protocol.

## Units

Units are standardized measures of the computational resources, such as processing power and memory, allocated to run your service. The quantity of units you assign determines your application's performance capacity and directly influences its cost.

### GB-s

Unit used to measure the RAM consumption of a container. It reflects the amount of memory consumed over time in seconds.

### vCPU

vCPU is the abbreviation for **v**irtual **C**entralized **P**rocessing **U**nit. A vCPU represents a portion or share of the underlying physical CPU assigned to a particular container.
The performance of a vCPU is determined by the percentage of time spent on the physical processor's core. It is possible to allocate different resource allowances on specific vCPUs for specific containers or virtual machines.

### mvCPU

A [vCPU](#vcpu) (Virtual Central Processing Unit) is equivalent to 1000 mvCPU.

### vCPU-s

Unit used to measure the resource consumption of a container. It reflects the amount of vCPU used over time in seconds.

This section contains usage limits that apply when using Serverless Containers.

| Resources                                         | Criteria       | Limits            | Scope                       |

| Invocation rate                                   | Max number     | 5000 per second   | Container                   |
| Concurrency                                       | Max            | 80                | Container Instance          |
| Max Scale (simultaneous Container instances)      | Max            | 200               | Container                   |
| CPU                                               | Min/max        | 70 to 6000 mvCPU  | Container                   |

| Environment variables                             | Max number     | 200               | Container + namespace       |
| Environment variables                             | Max size       | 65536 chars       | Environment variable        |
| Secret environment variables                      | Max number     | 200               | Container + namespace       |
| Secret environment variables                      | Max size       | 65536 bytes       | Secret environment variable |
| Time before scale to zero                         | Time           | 15 minutes        | Instance                    |
| Time before scale down                            | Time           | 30 seconds        | Instance                    |
| HTTP request duration (timeout)\***               | Min/max        | 10 seconds to 60 minutes | Request              |
| Private Networks attached                         | Max            | 1                 | Container                   |
| Logs                                              | Logs           | 30000 per minute  | Project                     |

\* Lower limits may apply before account verification. Contact our Support team if you have any questions.

\** Total container memory is the sum of the memory allocated to all your containers at their maximum Scale.

\*** Use [Serverless Jobs](/serverless-jobs/) for tasks up to 24h.

These limits are enforced as [Organization quotas](/organizations-and-projects/organization/organization-quotas/#serverless-containers).

During the execution of the container, if the limits are exceeded, a restart occurs.

## Image size

We recommend keeping your image size **below 1 GB** to ensure faster deployment and better cold start performance.

### Tips for keeping image size down

* Use lightweight distribution like *Alpine*
* Minimize layers and unnecessary dependencies
* Clean up temp files and cache (e.g., `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` in Debian-based images)
* Use multi-stage builds to keep only runtime essentials. Examples:

<Tabs>
    <TabsTab label="Node.js">
    ```dockerfile
    # Build stage
    FROM node:22-alpine AS builder

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy package files
    COPY package*.json ./

    # Install dependencies
    RUN npm ci --only=production

    # Copy source code
    COPY . .

    # Runtime stage
    FROM node:22-alpine

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy built artifacts from builder
    COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
    COPY --from=builder /app .

    # Expose the port the app listens on
    ENV PORT=8080

    # Start the application
    CMD ["node", "index.js"]
    ```
    </TabsTab>
    <TabsTab label="Go">
    ```dockerfile
    # Build stage
    FROM golang:1.23-alpine AS builder

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy Go module files
    COPY go.mod go.sum ./

    # Download dependencies
    RUN go mod download

    # Copy source code
    COPY . .

    # Build the binary
    RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -a -installsuffix cgo -o main .

    # Runtime stage
    FROM scratch

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy the binary from builder
    COPY --from=builder /app/main .

    # Expose the port the app listens on
    ENV PORT=8080

    # Run the binary
    CMD ["./main"]
    ```
    </TabsTab>

    <TabsTab label="Python">
    ```dockerfile
    # Build stage
    FROM python:3.13-slim AS builder

    WORKDIR /app

    # Install build dependencies
    RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        gcc \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

    # Copy requirements and install dependencies
    COPY requirements.txt .
    RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt

    # Runtime stage
    FROM python:3.13-slim

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy installed packages from builder
    COPY --from=builder /root/.local /root/.local
    COPY . .

    # Make sure scripts in .local are usable
    ENV PATH=/root/.local/bin:$PATH

    # Expose the port the app listens on
    ENV PORT=8080

    # Run the application
    CMD ["python", "app.py"]
    ```
    </TabsTab>
    <TabsTab label="Rust">
    ```dockerfile
    # Build stage
    FROM rust:1.94-alpine AS builder

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy Cargo configuration
    COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock ./

    RUN mkdir src && \

        cargo build --release && \
        rm -rf src

    # Copy the actual source code
    COPY src ./src

    # Build the application
    RUN cargo build --release

    # Runtime stage
    FROM scratch

    WORKDIR /app

    # Copy the compiled binary from the builder stage
    COPY --from=builder /app/target/release/my-app .

    # Expose the port the app listens on
    ENV PORT=8080

    # Run the binary
    CMD ["./my-app"]

In order to ensure the proper functioning of the product, we restrict the use of certain ports and environment variables

### Blocked ports

Due to potential abuse (spam), no outbound traffic is allowed through the following ports, except from Scaleway Transactional Email SMTP servers.

* **25**
* **465**

### Unavailable custom ports
Do not have your containers listen on these ports, as they are used by our service.

title: Containers concurrency
description: Learn about concurrency settings for Scaleway Serverless Containers.
dates:
  validation: 2025-10-23
  posted: 2024-03-26
tags: serverless containers concurrency concurrent execution scaling parallelism parallel instances
---

## Concurrency overview

Concurrency determines the number of incoming requests a single instance of a container can process before scaling up. Serverless Containers automatically scale according to the number of instances needed to handle the incoming workload.

Unlike Serverless Functions, which handles only one request per instance, Serverless Containers is designed to handle multiple requests simultaneously within one container. This is a powerful feature for optimizing performance and reducing costs.

A higher number of instances processing requests at the same time implies a greater usage of memory and [vCPU](/serverless-containers/concepts/#vcpu), and consequently a higher cost.

```
                Concurrency = 1

                  ┌─────────────┐
                  │     ┌──────┐│
            │     │     │      ││
            └─────┼───► │      ││                   Concurrency = 80
                  │     │      ││
                  │     └──────┘│                    ┌─────────────┐
                  │     ┌──────┐│               │    │     ┌──────┐│
                  │     │      ││               └────┼───► │      ││
3 requests  ──────┼───► │      ││   3 requests  ─────┼───► │      ││
                  │     │      ││               ┌────┼───► │      ││
                  │     └──────┘│               │    │     └──────┘│
                  │     ┌──────┐│                    └─────────────┘
                  │     │      ││                       1 service
            ┌─────┼───► │      ││                 1 container instance
            │     │     │      ││
                  │     └──────┘│
                  └─────────────┘
                     1 service
               3 container instances
```

## Concurrency setting

When [deploying a container](/serverless-containers/how-to/deploy-container/), Scaleway Serverless Containers allows you to configure the [concurrency](/serverless-containers/concepts/#concurrency), which is the maximum number of requests a single container instance can handle at the same time. By default, Serverless Containers allow **80 concurrent requests** per container instance. We recommend using the default value, as Serverless Containers are designed to efficiently function with it, but you can lower it to better fit specific requirements.

## Impact of concurrency on container scaling

If the number of incoming requests exceeds the set concurrency value for a container, Serverless Containers automatically creates new container instances to handle the additional load.

For example, if a container is set to handle 10 concurrent requests, and 50 requests or events arrive at the same time, Serverless Containers will create at least 5 container instances to handle the incoming load.

## Benefits of concurrency

**Efficiency**: Setting a higher concurrency value allows a single container instance to handle more requests, which can reduce the total number of container instances, therefore reducing costs.

**Responsiveness**: Setting a lower concurrency (down to 1 concurrent container instance) allows you to reduce latency for individual requests, since the container focuses on fewer tasks at a time.

## Implications for your service

**Compute-bound workloads**: Workloads relying on heavy CPU or memory usage per request benefit from lower concurrency (e.g., 1 or 2) to avoid resource contention within the container.

**I/O-bound workloads**: Workloads relying on smaller input/output operations, such as waiting for external APIs or databases benefit from higher concurrency, since the container can handle multiple requests while waiting on I/O.

## Examples

### Low concurrency

If your Serverless Container hosts a resource-intensive application that can only handle a small number of requests with the provisioned memory and vCPU, you can reduce the number of maximum concurrent requests per instance to scale quicker and avoid bottlenecks and queued requests.

You can set the **Maximum concurrent requests per instance** of your container to `1` if it is designed to handle a single request at a time. However, a low maximum concurrency value may affect the performance of your deployment, as several instances of your container will start if it receives a high number of concurrent requests.

### High concurrency

If your Serverless Container hosts an application that receives a high number of requests that are easily processed with the provisioned memory and vCPU, you can set a greater number of maximum concurrent requests per instance.

By setting a greater concurrency value than the average number of concurrent requests your container can handle, it will only scale up in the event of a spike in received requests.---

import Requirements from '@macros/iam/requirements.mdx'


This page explains how to secure your container.

<Requirements />

- A Scaleway account logged into the [console](https://console.scaleway.com)
- [Owner](/iam/concepts/glossary/#owner) status or [IAM permissions](/iam/concepts/glossary/#permission) allowing you to perform actions in the intended Organization
- [Created a containers namespace](/serverless-containers/how-to/create-manage-delete-containers-namespace/)
- [Deployed a container](/serverless-containers/how-to/deploy-container/)
- Created an [authentication token](/serverless-containers/how-to/create-auth-token-from-console/) for your container
- [Created a Private Network](/vpc/how-to/create-private-network/) (only for using private endpoints)

## Use secrets to store access keys and sensitive information

To inject data into Serverless Containers, you can use:
* [Environment variables](/serverless-containers/concepts/#environment-variables) for general purpose data.
* [Secret environment variables](/serverless-containers/concepts/#secrets) for sensitive data.

### Configure secrets from the Scaleway console

1. In the [Scaleway console](https://console.scaleway.com) side menu, go to **Serverless** > **Containers**. The **Serverless Containers** page appears.
2. Click the relevant Containers namespace.
3. Click the name of the container for which you want to define secrets.
4. Click the **Deployment** tab.
5. Scroll to the **Secrets** section of the page and click **Add secret**. Enter the key and value for your secret. Repeat for additional secrets.
    <Message type="important">
        Be careful when you type your secrets. You will not be able to read the value in the console once submitted.
    </Message>
6. Click **Deploy container** to submit your secrets and redeploy your container.

### Configure secrets using the Serverless framework

Add `secret` to your container's description (more information in the [plugin documentation](https://github.com/scaleway/serverless-scaleway-functions#security-and-secret-management)).
We recommend using them with global environment variables or a `.env` file stored independently (and kept secret).

```
secret:
      secret_1: ${env:SCW_SECRET_KEY}
```
<Message type="important">
    We strongly suggest that you do not commit this in a Version Control System (VCS), and do not share your Project ID or access key. This helps to ensure the security of your configuration file, which may contain sensitive data.
</Message>

### Configure secrets using Terraform/OpenTofu

Add the following [resource description](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/scaleway/scaleway/latest/docs/resources/container) in Terraform/OpenTofu:

```hcl
secret_environment_variables = { "key" = "secret" }
```

## Restrict access to your containers

You can set Serverless containers as private if you want, to protect them from unwanted or unauthorized calls.

Unauthenticated calls will be rejected, and your container will not receive the incoming request.

### Restrict access by requiring an `X-Auth-Token`

1. In the [Scaleway console](https://console.scaleway.com) side menu, go to **Serverless** > **Containers**. The **Serverless Containers** page appears.
2. Click the relevant container namespace.
3. Click the name of the container for which you want to define secrets.
4. Click the **Security** tab.
5. Set the **Privacy Policy** of the container to **Private**.
6. If required, set up [IAM authentication](/serverless-containers/how-to/create-auth-token-from-console/) for your container.

Your container is now private, and requires an `X-Auth-Token` header to be called:

```bash
curl -H "X-Auth-Token: <YOUR_SECRET_KEY>" <YOUR_CONTAINER_ENDPOINT>
```

<Message type="important">
JWT authentication is deprecated, you must [migrate your existing containers to IAM authentication](/serverless-containers/how-to/migrate-jwt-to-iam-authentication/).
</Message>

### Restrict access using Private Networks

Using only a private endpoint allows your container to communicate only with other resources attached to Private Networks within the same VPC.

1. Attach your container to a [Private Network](/serverless-containers/how-to/use-private-networks/).
2. Enable the private endpoint for your container. 
3. Disable the public endpoint for your container. This prevents your container from being accessed from the public internet.


<Message type="tip">
    Private endpoints are compatible with `X-Auth-Token` authentication.
</Message>

## Advanced access control with IAM conditions

When a container is set to **Private**, you can use Scaleway IAM policy conditions to define granular access rules using Common Expression Language (CEL): [policy conditions documentation](/iam/policies-permissions/understanding-policy-conditions/).
These conditions use **Common Expression Language (CEL)** to evaluate requests based on attributes like IP address, time, or user-agent.

<Message type="note">
  IAM conditions are not global Access Control Lists (ACLs) for the service itself; they are restrictions applied to a specific policy rule.
  * **Policy-based**: A condition only restricts the specific IAM policy it is attached to.
  * **Owner exception**: Users with [Owner status](/iam/concepts/glossary/#owner) possess full administrative rights through global organization policies. Even if your custom policies include IP restrictions, an API key belonging to an Owner can still call the container from any IP address.
</Message>

### Restrict access to specific user-agents

You can restrict calls to specific tools or internal clients by checking the `request.user_agent` attribute. This is useful for ensuring only authorized automation tools (like Terraform or a specific internal bot) can trigger the service.

**Example expression:**

```cel
request.user_agent.contains("InternalAdminTool/1.0")
```

title: How to migrate from JWT to IAM authentication for private containers
description: Guide to transitioning from JWT authentication to IAM authentication via policies and API keys for Scaleway Serverless Containers.
tags: containers secure private api key jwt json web token migrate switch change iam secret key
dates:
  validation: 2025-11-24
  posted: 2025-11-24
---

<Message type="important">
  - The authentication method with existing tokens remains available. Only the creation of new tokens will no longer be supported
  - Creating new JWT tokens will be gradually deprecated, migrating to IAM tokens is strongly encouraged as JWT creation will be disabled during 2026
</Message>

Scaleway Serverless Functions and Containers used to rely on [legacy JWT authentication tokens](/serverless-containers/concepts/#jwt-token-legacy) to access private resources.

This feature is now deprecated, you must therefore use Scaleway IAM to access your private functions and containers using an [API key](/iam/credentials/create-api-keys/). This change allows for a better Scaleway ecosystem integration. Read the documentation on [advanced access control with IAM conditions](/serverless-containers/how-to/secure-a-container/#advanced-access-control-with-iam-conditions) for more information.

1. [Set up IAM authentication](/serverless-containers/how-to/create-auth-token-from-console/) by creating an IAM application and an API key associated with it, then grant the application the `FunctionsPrivateAccess` or `ContainersPrivateAccess` permission via an IAM policy.

2. [Delete the existing JWT](/serverless-containers/how-to/create-auth-token-from-console/#revoking-authentication/) for your Serverless Functions / Containers to revoke legacy authentication.

3. Pass the secret key of your IAM application's API key via the `X-Auth-Token` header to call your private resource:

```bash
curl -H "X-Auth-Token: <YOUR_SECRET_KEY>" <YOUR_ENDPOINT>
```

<Message type="note">
- Existing tokens will continue to work
- Reading (`GET`/`LIST`) and deleting (`DELETE`) JWT tokens will remain available for the next months
- No application code changes are required, only header value updates are needed
</Message>

## Granularity changes with IAM tokens

The JWT system allows you to create tokens for specific Serverless Namespaces and Serverless Functions and Containers. IAM tokens are scoped by projects, meaning the level of granularity will change.

To preserve the level of granularity when required, it is recommended to separate your resources within different projects.

<Message type="note">
**While IAM granularity is not available, JWT system will continue to work**

Improvements are underway regarding IAM to provide a system with the same level of granularity as JWT.
</Message>

## Motivations of changes

When Scaleway Serverless Functions and Containers was first developed, IAM was not yet available as a service. To provide secure access to private Functions and Containers, we implemented JWT authentication as the primary authentication mechanism.

However, with the introduction and maturation of IAM, Scaleway now has a more robust and integrated authentication system. Migrating from JWT to IAM offers several advantages:

- **Better ecosystem integration**: IAM is deeply integrated with all Scaleway services, providing consistent authentication and authorization patterns across the platform
- **Enhanced security features**: IAM benefits from ongoing security improvements and follows best practices for authentication
- **Rapid evolution**: IAM is actively developed and will receive frequent updates and new features, ensuring your authentication system stays current
- **Unified management**: Using IAM for authentication centralizes access control management across all Scaleway resources

As IAM continues to evolve rapidly, it will offer capabilities that improve what the legacy JWT system could provide, making it the preferred authentication method for Serverless Functions and Containers.

"""TEST-ONLY loopback HTTP hosting probe. No Strands, provider calls or run effects.

Synthetic /probe routes deliberately do NOT implement runtime-http/events v1.
In-memory ownership, retention and semaphore are not production auth/storage.
"""
from contextlib import contextmanager
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
import hmac
import json
import secrets
import threading
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qs


class MemorySessions:
    """Seeded synthetic state; never persists secrets, mandates or paid effects."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = {"session-a": {"owner": "alice", "events": [1, 2, 3]}}
        self.available = True

    def read(self, session_id, owner):
        if not self.available:
            return 503, None
        row = self.rows.get(session_id)
        if row is None:
            return 410, None
        if row["owner"] != owner:
            return 403, None
        return 200, row


class ProbeServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = False
    block_on_close = True

    def __init__(self, sessions=None, duration=0.3, capacity=2):
        self.sessions = sessions if sessions is not None else MemorySessions()
        self.duration = duration
        self.interval = 0.025
        self.stop = threading.Event()
        self.slots = threading.BoundedSemaphore(capacity)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.active = 0
        self.peak = 0
        self.tokens = {secrets.token_hex(32): "alice", secrets.token_hex(32): "bob"}
        super().__init__(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.expected_host = "127.0.0.1:" + str(self.server_port)

    def handle_error(self, request, client_address):
        # Never log exception/request contents in this synthetic probe.
        pass


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def reply(self, status, code, payload=None):
        data = json.dumps({"code": code} if payload is None else payload).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)
        self.close_connection = True

    def do_GET(self):
        self.connection.settimeout(0.5)  # Bound a blocked write/read in test harness.
        server = self.server
        if self.client_address[0] != "127.0.0.1":
            return self.reply(403, "forbidden")
        if (self.headers.get_all("Host") != [server.expected_host]
                or self.headers.get_all("Origin") is not None):
            return self.reply(403, "forbidden")
        auth = self.headers.get_all("Authorization") or []
        owner = None
        if len(auth) == 1:
            for token, identity in server.tokens.items():
                if hmac.compare_digest(auth[0], "Bearer " + token):
                    owner = identity
        if owner is None:
            return self.reply(401, "unauthorized")
        parsed = urlsplit(self.path)
        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc or parsed.fragment:
            return self.reply(400, "invalid_request")
        query = parse_qs(parsed.query, keep_blank_values=True)
        if parsed.path == "/probe/health" and not query:
            return self.reply(200, "ok")
        if parsed.path == "/probe/events" and not query:
            return self.stream()
        if parsed.path == "/probe/sessions/session-a":
            if set(query) - {"after"} or any(len(v) != 1 for v in query.values()):
                return self.reply(400, "invalid_request")
            cursor = query.get("after", ["0"])[0]
            if not cursor.isascii() or not cursor.isdigit() or len(cursor) > 6:
                return self.reply(400, "invalid_request")
            cursor = int(cursor)
            ids = self.headers.get_all("Last-Event-ID")
            if ids is not None and ids != [str(cursor)]:
                return self.reply(400, "invalid_request")
            status, row = server.sessions.read("session-a", owner)
            if status != 200:
                return self.reply(status, {403: "forbidden", 410: "replay_unavailable", 503: "store_unavailable"}[status])
            # Retain only last two events; no relaunch on evicted cursor.
            if cursor < row["events"][-2] - 1:
                return self.reply(410, "replay_unavailable")
            if cursor > row["events"][-1]:
                return self.reply(400, "invalid_request")
            return self.reply(200, "ok", {"events": [n for n in row["events"][-2:] if n > cursor]})
        return self.reply(400, "invalid_request")

    def stream(self):
        server = self.server
        if not server.slots.acquire(blocking=False):
            return self.reply(429, "capacity_exceeded")
        with server.lock:
            server.active += 1
            server.peak = max(server.peak, server.active)
        try:
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
            self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-transform")
            self.send_header("Connection", "close")
            self.end_headers()
            self.close_connection = True
            start = time.monotonic()
            sequence = 1
            self.wfile.write(b'id: 1\nevent: probe\ndata: {"kind":"started"}\n\n')
            self.wfile.flush()
            while not server.stop.wait(server.interval):
                if time.monotonic() - start >= server.duration:
                    sequence += 1
                    data = ('id: %d\nevent: probe\ndata: {"kind":"deadline","remote_outcome":"not_sent"}\n\n' % sequence).encode()
                    self.wfile.write(data)
                    self.wfile.flush()
                    break
                self.wfile.write(b': heartbeat\n\n')
                self.wfile.flush()
        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, TimeoutError):
            # Transport disconnection stops only this synthetic stream, no rollback.
            pass
        finally:
            with server.lock:
                server.active -= 1
            server.slots.release()


@contextmanager
def running_probe(**kwargs):
    server = ProbeServer(**kwargs)
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.01})
    thread.start()
    try:
        yield server
    finally:
        server.stop.set()
        server.shutdown()
        server.server_close()
        thread.join(timeout=2)
        if thread.is_alive() or server.active:
            raise RuntimeError("probe cleanup failed")

title: Serverless Containers HTTP headers reference
description: This page provides a detailed reference of the HTTP headers injected into requests for Scaleway Serverless Containers.
tags: serverless containers headers http request-id proxy
dates:
  validation: 2026-04-22
  posted: 2026-04-22
---

Scaleway Serverless Containers automatically inject several HTTP headers into every incoming request. These headers provide metadata about the request, the client, and the routing path through the Scaleway infrastructure.

You can use these headers within your container logic for logging, security, and request tracing.

## Injected headers reference

The following headers are available in the request object of your container.

| Header | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `X-Forwarded-For` | A standard header used to identify the originating IP address of a client connecting through an HTTP proxy or load balancer. |
| `X-Forwarded-Proto` | A header indicating the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) used by the client to connect to the container. |
| `X-Real-IP` | A header containing the IP of the container caller. Scaleway overwrites this header even if it has been explicitly passed. |
| `X-Request-ID` | A unique string assigned to each incoming request to facilitate tracing and debugging. |

<Message type="note">
  If there is one or more proxies between the client and the container, the `X-Real-IP` header contains the IP address of the last proxy, not the client. To retrieve the client IP address, use the `X-Forwarded-For` header instead. Clients can modify the `X-Forwarded-For` value, so do not rely on it for security purposes.

The `X-Request-ID` header is essential for distributed tracing. Each request receives a unique identifier that persists throughout the lifecycle of the request within the Scaleway ecosystem.

Keep four concerns separate: **project classification**, **Git commit identity**, **GitHub API identity**, and **npm registry credentials**. A matching username alone never proves package access; verify the intended capability against the intended registry.

Classify from the canonical absolute project root, not the shell's transient cwd:

| Context | Git config | GitHub account | npm registry/scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Personal | ~/.gitconfig-personal | bioinfornatics | npmjs, @bioinfornatics/* |

Never print tokens. Redact auth lines and report only presence/source.

# Repository Context Audit

Use this skill at the start of work in an unfamiliar repository or whenever the current working directory may be wrong.

## Purpose

Avoid acting in the wrong repository, using the wrong personal/professional identity, or applying commands to an empty/non-git directory.

## First commands

Use code exploration tools after the context audit when:

Use Beads as the shared project task system. Local plans, scratch files, and personal memories are useful, but they are not the durable source of truth for project work.

bd where

Use the `bd` CLI when shell access is available. It is the most compact and direct Beads interface.

bd ready

bd list --status=in_progress

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```

**Note:** No git remote configured. Issues are saved locally only.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: local-only (no git remote)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

class MemorySessions:
    """Seeded synthetic state; never persists secrets, mandates or paid effects."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = {"session-a": {"owner": "alice", "events": [1, 2, 3]}}
        self.available = True

    def read(self, session_id, owner):
        if not self.available:
            return 503, None
        row = self.rows.get(session_id)
        if row is None:
            return 410, None
        if row["owner"] != owner:

class ProbeServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):

        self.interval = 0.025
        self.stop = threading.Event()
        self.slots = threading.BoundedSemaphore(capacity)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```

**Note:** No git remote configured. Issues are saved locally only.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: local-only (no git remote)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

Revision: 0.1 — 2026-10-20. Status: stakeholder-requested concept; proposed scope and defaults, not validated user research or implementation approval.

<a id="vision"></a>
## Vision

Enable developers to move from a Scaleway model experiment to a reproducible, evaluated and inspectable AI application from their existing VS Code workspace. Equivalent developer workflows to Microsoft Foundry Toolkit are the objective; literal Azure-service parity and menu cloning are not.

<a id="users"></a>
## Users and shared outcome

Primary responsibility: an AI/application developer must select a model, test a prompt, implement bounded tools, establish application quality and deliver runnable code.
Complementary responsibility: a platform operator must control credentials, deployment scope, spend, execution rights and operational recovery. These are responsibilities, not researched personas.
Shared service boundary: VS Code extension, local generated application/runtime and explicitly selected Scaleway resources. External MCP servers and retrieval backends are separate trust boundaries.
Shared outcome: a working application with reproducible configuration, inspectable runs and identifiable resources that can be cleaned up.

<a id="value"></a>
## Value hypothesis and current alternative

Current alternative (inferred): Scaleway console playground plus SDK scripts, terminal/container commands and separate dashboards. Existing console/SDK capabilities may already be sufficient; compare against them fairly.
Hypothesis: the extension reduces total effort from model selection to useful, reproducible application output, including credential setup, verification, corrections and switching overhead. Frequency, demand, willingness to maintain and measurable advantage are unknown.
Observable first-slice outcome: starting with an authorized account and a VS Code workspace, the developer connects, selects a supported model, completes a streaming test, saves the prompt and runs exported code outside the extension. No secrets appear in workspace files, UI messages or captured logs.
The extension is a deterministic development workbench, not a mandatory coding chatbot. AI is the application/model under test; direct controls remain available. A single impressive response is not quality evidence.

<a id="scope"></a>
## Capabilities and staged scope

Phase 0: verify API contracts, selected Strands Python/Scaleway compatibility, security boundaries, developer value and hosting constraints.
Phase 1/MVP: secure connection, model catalog, streaming playground, saved experiments, Python/TypeScript export and read-only dedicated deployment browsing.
Phase 2: portable agent specification, one Strands Python SDK-backed local HTTP runtime, user-approved MCP tools, inspector and evaluations. SDK selection accepted by stakeholder; compatibility and safety unverified.
Phase 3: dedicated model deployment and containerized agent application hosting, hosted playground, status/logs, trace integration and cleanup.
Phase 4: retrieval backends, additional runtimes/providers and fine-tuning only after demand and feasibility are verified.
Non-goals for MVP: Foundry Agent Service compatibility, native Scaleway agent/thread/vector-store claims, fine-tuning, ONNX conversion, Windows profiling, autonomous cloud management, multi-framework runtime parity and marketplace publication.

<a id="principles"></a>
## Product principles and constraints

- Portable outputs: saved specifications and exported code remain useful without VS Code.
- Truthful resources: model deployment is not agent hosting; an object bucket is not a vector search service.
- Capability-aware controls: unsupported or unknown model features are not shown as supported.
- Context before action: make connection, project, region, endpoint and effects visible.
- Bound execution: budgets, steps, concurrency, cancellation and explicit tool mandates.
- Safe defaults: no navigation-triggered execution, secret leakage or automatic billable resource creation.
- Progressive disclosure: native resource trees and task navigation; focused editor workspaces, not a dashboard of equal-weight panels.
- VS Code-native design: theme tokens, native icons/trees, keyboard access, focus management and high-contrast compatibility. No supplied official Scaleway design system or brand template.

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```

**Note:** No git remote configured. Issues are saved locally only.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: local-only (no git remote)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

import * as vscode from 'vscode';
import { models, DemoModel, Experiment, runDemo } from './demo';

export function activate(context: vscode.ExtensionContext): void {
  const output = vscode.window.createOutputChannel('Scaleway AI — Offline Playground');
  let selected: DemoModel = models[0];
  let last: Experiment | undefined;
  let active: {cancelled: boolean} | undefined;
  const changed = new vscode.EventEmitter<void>();
  const provider: vscode.TreeDataProvider<DemoModel> = {
    onDidChangeTreeData: changed.event,
    getChildren: () => [...models],
    getParent: () => undefined,
    getTreeItem: model => {
      const item = new vscode.TreeItem(model.label, vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.None);
      item.description = selected.id === model.id ? 'Selected · offline' : 'Offline';
      item.tooltip = model.description + '. Click to select this synthetic model.';
      item.iconPath = new vscode.ThemeIcon(selected.id === model.id ? 'check' : 'symbol-method');
      item.command = {command: 'scalewayAI.select', title: 'Select model', arguments: [model.id]};
      return item;
    },
  };
  const view = vscode.window.createTreeView('scalewayAI.models', {treeDataProvider: provider});
  view.message = 'Offline preview · synthetic models · no credentials or charges';
  const status = vscode.window.createStatusBarItem(vscode.StatusBarAlignment.Left, 20);
  status.text = '$(beaker) Scaleway AI: Offline';
  status.tooltip = 'Open experimental offline model playground';
  status.command = 'scalewayAI.open'; status.show();
  const register = (id: string, callback: (...args: any[]) => unknown) =>
    context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand(id, callback));
  register('scalewayAI.select', (id: unknown) => {
    const model = models.find(item => item.id === id);
    if (!model) return;
    selected = model; changed.fire();
  });
  register('scalewayAI.open', async () => {
    await vscode.commands.executeCommand('workbench.view.extension.scalewayAI');
    await view.reveal(selected, {select: true, focus: true});
  });
  register('scalewayAI.cancel', () => { if (active) active.cancelled = true; });
  register('scalewayAI.experiment', async () => {
    if (!last) { void vscode.window.showInformationMessage('Run the offline playground first.'); return; }
    const document = await vscode.workspace.openTextDocument({language: 'json', content: JSON.stringify(last, null, 2)});
    await vscode.window.showTextDocument(document, {preview: false});
    // Untitled document only: user chooses whether/where to save prompt/output.
  });
  register('scalewayAI.playground', async () => {
    if (active) { void vscode.window.showInformationMessage('A demo is running. Cancel it before starting another.'); return; }
    const prompt = await vscode.window.showInputBox({
      title: 'Scaleway AI — Offline Playground', prompt: 'Synthetic stream only. Nothing is sent to Scaleway.',
      placeHolder: 'Explain what this toolkit will do', ignoreFocusOut: true,
      validateInput: value => !value.trim() || Buffer.byteLength(value, 'utf8') > 4096 ? 'Enter 1–4096 UTF-8 bytes.' : undefined,
    });
    if (prompt === undefined) return;
    if (active) return;
    const run = {cancelled: false}; active = run;
    output.clear(); output.appendLine('OFFLINE SYNTHETIC DEMO — no API, no billing');
    output.appendLine('Model: ' + selected.label); output.appendLine(''); output.show(true);
    try {
      await vscode.window.withProgress({location: vscode.ProgressLocation.Notification,
        title: 'Scaleway AI: Simulating stream', cancellable: true}, async (_progress, token) => {
        const subscription = token.onCancellationRequested(() => { run.cancelled = true; });
        try {
          last = await runDemo(selected, prompt, () => run.cancelled || token.isCancellationRequested, chunk => output.append(chunk));
          output.appendLine(''); output.appendLine('Demo ' + last.status + '. No inference was sent.');
        } finally { subscription.dispose(); }
      });
    } catch {
      void vscode.window.showErrorMessage('Offline demo failed. No network request was made.');
    } finally { if (active === run) active = undefined; }
  });
  context.subscriptions.push(output, view, status, changed, {dispose: () => {
    if (active) active.cancelled = true;
    last = undefined;
  }});
}

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```

**Note:** No git remote configured. Issues are saved locally only.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: local-only (no git remote)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

import {models, DemoModel, Experiment, runDemo} from './demo';
import {parseInput} from './ipc';
import {playgroundHtml} from './webview';

interface Node {id: string; label: string; icon?: string; command?: string; args?: unknown[]; children?: Node[]; description?: string;}
export function activate(context: vscode.ExtensionContext): void {
  let selected: DemoModel = models[0];
  let last: Experiment | undefined;
  let active: {cancelled: boolean} | undefined;
  let panel: vscode.WebviewPanel | undefined;
  let response = '';
  let message = 'Prêt · Ctrl+Entrée pour exécuter';
  const changed = new vscode.EventEmitter<void>();
  const refresh = () => changed.fire();
  const update = () => {
    void panel?.webview.postMessage({type: 'state', model: selected.id, running: !!active,
      output: response || 'La réponse simulée apparaîtra ici.', status: message, hasExperiment: !!last});
    void vscode.commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'scalewayAI.running', !!active);
  };
  const modelNodes = (): Node[] => models.map(m => ({id: m.id, label: m.label.replace('Demo · ', ''),
    icon: selected.id === m.id ? 'check' : 'symbol-method', description: selected.id === m.id ? 'Sélectionné' : 'Synthétique',
    command: 'scalewayAI.select', args: [m.id]}));
  const resources = (): Node[] => [
    {id: 'mode', label: 'Démonstration hors ligne', icon: 'beaker'},
    {id: 'models', label: 'Modèles de démonstration', icon: 'library', children: modelNodes()},
    {id: 'last', label: 'Dernière expérience', icon: 'history', description: last ? last.status : 'Aucune', command: 'scalewayAI.experiment'},
  ];
  const tools = (): Node[] => [
    {id: 'discover', label: 'Découvrir', children: [{id: 'catalog', label: 'Catalogue de démonstration', icon: 'library', command: 'scalewayAI.catalog'}]},
    {id: 'build', label: 'Construire et tester', children: [{id: 'playground', label: 'Playground modèle', icon: 'beaker', command: 'scalewayAI.playground'}]},
  ];
  const help = (): Node[] => [
    {id: 'start', label: 'Bien démarrer', icon: 'book', command: 'scalewayAI.getStarted'},
    {id: 'docs', label: 'Documentation Scaleway', icon: 'link-external', command: 'scalewayAI.documentation'},
  ];
  const createView = (id: string, roots: () => Node[]) => {
    const provider: vscode.TreeDataProvider<Node> = {
      onDidChangeTreeData: changed.event,
      getChildren: node => node?.children ?? roots(),
      getParent: () => undefined,
      getTreeItem: node => {
        const item = new vscode.TreeItem(node.label, node.children ? vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.Expanded : vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.None);
        item.id = node.id; item.description = node.description;
        if (node.icon) item.iconPath = new vscode.ThemeIcon(node.icon);
        if (node.command) item.command = {command: node.command, title: node.label, arguments: node.args};
        return item;
      },
    };
    const view = vscode.window.createTreeView(id, {treeDataProvider: provider});
    context.subscriptions.push(view); return view;
  };
  createView('scalewayAI.models', resources);
  createView('scalewayAI.tools', tools);
  createView('scalewayAI.help', help);
  const register = (id: string, callback: (...args: any[]) => unknown) =>
    context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand(id, callback));
  const openExperiment = async () => {
    if (!last) { void vscode.window.showInformationMessage('Exécutez une démonstration pour créer une expérience.'); return; }
    const doc = await vscode.workspace.openTextDocument({language: 'json', content: JSON.stringify(last, null, 2)});
    await vscode.window.showTextDocument(doc, {preview: false});
  };
  const execute = async (model: string, prompt: string) => {
    if (active || !panel) return;
    const found = models.find(m => m.id === model); if (!found) return;
    selected = found;
    const run = {cancelled: false}; active = run;
    const origin = panel;
    response = ''; message = 'Réponse simulée en cours…'; refresh(); update();
    try {
      const result = await runDemo(selected, prompt, () => run.cancelled, chunk => {
        if (active !== run || panel !== origin) return;
        response += chunk; update();
      });
      if (panel === origin && active === run) {
        last = result; message = result.status === 'completed' ? 'Démonstration terminée · aucun appel API' : 'Démonstration arrêtée · réponse partielle';
      }
    } catch { if (panel === origin) message = 'Instruction invalide ou démonstration interrompue.'; }
    finally { if (active === run) active = undefined; refresh(); update(); }

## Endpoint/authentication/scope

scw-models 13–23 documents GET https://api.scaleway.ai/v1/models, Bearer auth and basic inference-model metadata. Not deployments, feature matrix, serving weights, lifecycle or quota discovery. No complete response schema/pagination established. scw-auth 13–31 requires Bearer secret key; 48–61 lists GenerativeApisModelAccess/GenerativeApisFullAccess/AllProductsFullAccess. Narrow query permission is a candidate, not proven sufficient for other operations; no broad privileges by default.

Developer projection lists GET /v1/models but POST /{project_id}/v1/chat/completions and similar project-scoped inference paths. Older docs use /v1/chat/completions. Optional/default-project semantics unresolved; this does not prove older URLs stopped working. Verify base path/project scope under separate approval, no fallback requests. Prose mentions Paris/fr-par/optional region path but operation projection contains project_id, not region. Hostname does not establish selectable region or residency. Native managed agent/thread/session catalog remains unknown.

scw-chat 55–85 lists messages/model, sampling, stream/stream_options/tools/tool_choice/response_format support; excludes frequency_penalty/n/top_logprobs/logit_bias/user. Developer description additionally excludes metadata/prompt_cache_key/store/audio output and other matrix-listed parameters. Incomplete overlapping lists do not prove parity: endpoint/model/API allowlist required; unknown options blocked or explicitly approved for experiments. Strands params does not filter Scaleway options.

scw-function-calling 302–320 documents streamed tools, not live model framing. scw-compatibility cumulative usage section explicitly applies to Dedicated Deployment; cannot establish serverless usage. Its “OpenAI never returns streaming usage” claim is stale relative to modern include_usage. Missing usage unknown, not zero; do not sum cumulative snapshots.

- 690–710 GPT-OSS 120b: generic tools Yes but Chat Completions tools explicitly unsupported, Responses recommended. Selected OpenAIModel uses Chat Completions: unsuitable tool-agent candidate under this transport; no silent Responses/SDK switch.

scw-lifecycle 16–35 permits redirecting retired strings to alternative models: same identifier does not prove same weights. PyPI strands-agents 1.61.1, Python >=3.10, tag python/v1.61.1, commit 5cb880559e5ed88bd55de2779e72d060020f756b reviewed. sdk-python API currently redirects to harness-sdk monorepo; strands-py SDK differs from harness-py. Validate final modified tools/arguments atomically against mandate/revocation/step/token/concurrency limits.

Agent.cancel/caller cancel_signal and cleanup support local safe-point cancellation, not immediate remote abort, billing stop, rollback or arbitrary synchronous tool interruption. Preserve partial output/unknown usage and accepted/unknown effects; reconcile before retry.

scw-errors 16–45 shows nested recent vs flat legacy envelopes (legacy sample lacks comma); 51–61 lists 400/401/403/404/422/429/500 and SSE errors after HTTP 200. Experimental community VS Code extension; no Scaleway affiliation. Real **read-only

## Install

    code --install-extension artifacts/scaleway-ai-toolkit-preview-0.0.3.vsix --force

Reload Window after updating. Run **Scaleway AI: Open Offline Preview** to open the
sidebar (legacy command name retained).

## Connect and switch project

1. Mes ressources -> **Projet : sélectionner** -> native connection wizard.
2. Enter connection name, **organization UUID**, then **secret API key** in the
   masked field. Obtain these yourself from Scaleway console; never paste keys
   into chat/workspace/settings. Use a narrowly scoped key, not full owner rights.
3. Confirm bounded read-only listing of that organization’s projects (max 5 GET).
4. Select an accessible project then **fr-par** for dedicated resources.
5. Under Modèles click **Charger / actualiser les modèles** and confirm the
   read-only request scope (max 6 GET: 1 global serverless + up to 5 dedicated pages).

**Changer de projet** reuses the saved key. **Se connecter / changer de connexion**
replaces it through the same wizard. **Se déconnecter** deletes the saved key and
connection metadata, cancels pending reads and clears resource lists. Workspace
Trust is required for network connection; expanding native trees/startup never
fetches. Only one connection is stored in this increment. Project/region selection
is session-only; after reload select the project again. Name and organization ID
are saved in extension globalState, outside workspace; key only in SecretStorage.
With remote VS Code, extension runs in workspace host and uses its SecretStorage;
this is not a claim of local-machine isolation.

The Serverless list is **global and accessible to the key**, not proven project
availability. Dedicated entries are existing deployments filtered by selected
project/organization and fr-par, not dedicated model catalog entries. Empty and
failed lists are distinct; other services can fail independently. Model click
shows scope info only: **real models cannot yet execute in the playground**.
No quotas/prices/features inferred from GET discovery. A 403 may mean IAM policy
missing, not invalid key; no broad privilege escalation or automatic fallback.

Transport is fixed to api.scaleway.com (X-Auth-Token) and api.scaleway.ai (Bearer).
No arbitrary endpoint, redirects, retries or environment proxy inheritance.
Each GET has 10s deadline and 2MiB body bound; collections max5 sequential pages.
No body/header/error details logged. Local adapters use strict minimum projections,
not complete provider schemas; duplicate JSON keys/full production parser hardening
and full IAM/quota/private endpoint acceptance remain separate work.

## Offline playground

Mes ressources -> Démonstration hors ligne -> choose synthetic model.
Outils de développement -> Construire et tester -> **Playground modèle**.
Enter prompt, Exécuter/Ctrl+Enter; response stays in the central editor. Arrêter
preserves partial output. Open experiment JSON, save only if desired. Closing
playground cancels demo. No prompt/output automatically saved, no credential ever
passed to webview. Help/documentation opens browser only when explicitly clicked.

## Build

    cd apps/vscode-extension
    npm ci --ignore-scripts
    npm run package

Private package; no publishing/tag/push. Tests use synthetic keys and mocked
provider/VS Code interfaces; real account access and user login are not proven by
those tests. Native Extension Host startup is separately checked without keys.
Next increment is selected-real-model playground under explicit bounded spend,
not another hosted-agent spike. Production/design/value gates remain separate
from the requested experimental incremental implementation.
